item.title: Re: Keter classification
item.content:encoded:
It is Keter because, despite being generally benign - perhaps extremely so, the anomaly can't be contained and, to compound on this, follows no predictable pattern that would allow the extrapolation of its occurrences.

The Object Class is determined by how difficult to contain something is; not exactly by how much of a threat it poses.

item.title: SCP-##########
item.content:encoded:
That is a 10 digit number….that means that the SCP would be (at the very least) SCP-1,000,000,000……We are still in the 3000 block….
So: What could it be?
Well, I recall the Monatak? protocol. I don't recall the number designation or even how to spell the word, but basically it was this lady that would "give birth" to….the end of the world. It also seems to borrow heavily from Revelations and the Seven Seals, and there were six women who "gave birth" previously…so this one will break the seventh seal…in theory?
The Seventh Seal and the Golden Censer "When he opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and to them were given seven trumpets….(et ecetra, et cetera)" Though, in my copy of the Bible…I don't see when the lamb broke the seventh seal…and due to the fact that Revelations is about the END of the world…well…it could be three thousand years from now.
If SCP-990 and the one with Monatak were REAL (which I sure as heck hope they are not, but ya know….) then I don't think that Monatak would be happening recently…it would assume that the events would have started some time after NOW as a massive, end of world begins event like that…well, you couldn't keep that a secret for long…but SCP-990 may already be here, predicting what will happen latter.
Just my little perspective on the subject. I don't really know if I got my point across, something I have trouble doing, but if I did then YA!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
No, it doesn't have to do with containment — not in the way you're describing, at least.

From Object Classes:

Keter-class objects are anomalies that pose an inimical threat to the safety of Foundation personnel and the rest of mankind and either require extensive and complex procedures to contain or cannot be fully contained by the Foundation's current technology and knowledge.

Notice the first part: "pose an inimical threat to the safety of Foundation personnel and the rest of mankind". That is certainly not proven in the case of SCP-990.

Contrast with the definition of the Euclid class:

Euclid-class objects are anomalies that are either insufficiently understood or inherently unpredictable, such that reliable containment is not always possible, but do not pose sufficient threat to qualify for Keter classification. The vast majority of anomalies cataloged and contained by the Foundation are initially classified as Euclid until they are either sufficiently understood or exhibit sufficient danger to qualify for reclassification.

So unless the skip clearly demonstrates that it poses a sufficient threat level to be considered inimical by its very nature to the Foundation in particular and humanity in general, the skip shouldn't be classified as Keter.

Besides, your own logic fails because we have about 60 skips right now that are both Euclid class and uncontained (do a tag-search if you don't believe me).

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Containment class isn't measured by hostility or potential danger; it's measured by difficulty of containment. A nuclear bomb would be classified as Safe, since even though it can be very dangerous, it won't do anything if you leave it alone. This guy is pretty much impossible to contain since he only appears in dreams, and thus he's Keter.
